title: Big questions: a first course in philosophy
purpose: Meet the central questions of philosophy through short readings and thought experiments: what we can know, whether the world is as it seems, what a mind is, whether we have free will, what makes you the same person over time, what time is, whether God exists and what makes actions right, practicing careful reading, discussion and short argumentative writing.

weeks.1: What is philosophy? Questions, arguments and thought experiments
weeks.2: How to read and discuss philosophy
weeks.3: Knowledge and skepticism: could you be dreaming?
weeks.4: Appearance and reality: is the world as it seems?
weeks.5: Minds: what is a mind, and could a computer have one?
weeks.6: Free will: are your choices up to you?
weeks.7: Personal identity: what makes you the same person over time?
weeks.8: Time: does the past still exist?
weeks.9: Does God exist? Classic arguments for and against
weeks.10: What exists? Numbers, colors, holes and shadows
weeks.11: Right and wrong: what makes an action right?
weeks.12: The meaning of life and how to live

blocks.deliverable: Write a paragraph about a big question that puzzles you.
Explain the dream argument and one reply.
Write one page on whether a robot could think.
Week 7 midterm; explain the ship of Theseus and two answers.
Summarize one argument for and one against God's existence fairly.
Write a one-page argument for your answer to one big question.
Submit the project; take an unseen 45 minute final in week 14.

project: Philosophy dialogue: write a three- to four-page dialogue between two characters who disagree about one big question from the course (free will, minds, personal identity, time or God), in which each gives at least two real arguments and answers the other's objections, then add a half-page note on which argument you find strongest and why.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
